about: Born, Not Made, tail copy variant (23 Nov 2026): the parent prints the two segments of a new tail and puts a new arm together from four floating modules. Frame: x toward the parent's mouth, y port, z up, meters, origin on the tank floor; the parent sits 200 mm back from the quilted head simulator.

tank.name: a 3.0 x 1.22 m tank (estimate: room for two tails side by side and one to turn)

stages.name: The parent and the parts
stages.text: The parent, a hard tail with its DexArm and a quilted head, sits in the middle of the tank. Four arm modules stand on a tray against the back glass: base, upper arm, forearm, end effector. No floats.

stages.name: Pods on the floor
stages.text: The holder lays N's two sealed pods on the floor of the bowl, the way it lays a kit: a battery and a Raspberry Pi in one, the pump in the other.

stages.name: Print N
stages.text: The needle prints the nose segment folded flat over the pods: 18 layers, 79 mm tall, double wall with the quilt between.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Dragon Skin 30 cures in the gel for 16 hours.

stages.name: Birth of N
stages.text: The holder lifts the folded nose out of the gel and pushes it over the lip. Outside, air goes into the quilt and the segment opens to its printed shape.

stages.name: N wakes
stages.text: The Pi in the pod boots on its own battery. N has the pump, so the first part of the child is the part that moves: it swims clear of the mouth.

stages.name: Print F
stages.text: The needle prints the face segment: a quilted ring with the arm's seat plate printed into its floor, 18 layers, 79 mm tall.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Sixteen hours in the gel.

stages.name: Birth of F
stages.text: F is born the same way. It has no pump: it opens in front of the mouth and waits.

stages.name: N moves F aside
stages.text: N pushes F against the port glass and parks itself against the starboard glass: the middle of the tank is clear.

stages.name: N docks to F
stages.text: N backs its open end onto F's rear cuff: magnets in the two cuffs, the same as the docking of a tail and a head. Pogo pads in the cuff carry the battery's power into F. The new tail is whole, still without an arm.

stages.name: The parent leaves its head
stages.text: The tilt release lets the nine magnets go. The parent's tail backs 250 mm away from its head on its wheels. The head stays where it is.

stages.name: It turns round
stages.text: It turns on the spot, its face now toward the back glass.

stages.name: To the tray
stages.text: It drives to the tray on the back glass, where the four modules of the new arm stand.

stages.name: The new tail comes round
stages.text: The new tail swims down the side of the tank, past the head, and waits beside the place of the handover.

stages.name: Module 1: base
stages.text: The base slides to the middle of the tray and the holder takes it. The parent drives back, the new tail comes in and docks face to face. It sets the base in F's seat: three magnets and the pogo pads. The new arm has power.

stages.name: Module 2: upper arm
stages.text: The upper arm slides to the middle of the tray and the holder takes it. The parent drives back, the new tail comes in and docks face to face. The new arm holds its shoulder up; the upper arm goes down onto it and clicks.

stages.name: Module 3: forearm
stages.text: The forearm slides to the middle of the tray and the holder takes it. The parent drives back, the new tail comes in and docks face to face. The new arm leans its upper arm toward the parent; the forearm clicks onto the elbow.

stages.name: Module 4: end effector
stages.text: The end effector slides to the middle of the tray and the holder takes it. The parent drives back, the new tail comes in and docks face to face. It holds its wrist where the parent can reach; the end effector clicks on. The arm is whole.

stages.name: Its own arm
stages.text: The new arm straightens to its rest pose, inside its own tail.

stages.name: Apart
stages.text: The magnets let go. The parent backs off; the new tail turns round to face the tray.

stages.name: It picks up the rest
stages.text: The new tail swims to the tray. With its own arm it takes the last thing there, a tile set, and puts it inside itself. From here it can gather what it needs.

stages.name: Two tails
stages.text: The parent turns and docks back to its head. The new tail has two quilted halves, an arm put together inside it, and a first thing it picked up itself.

notes: The tail splits where the hard tail is already printed in two on the H2S (x = -215 mm). Each half has less skin than a head (0.170 and 0.281 against 0.328 m2), so each folds into the head's own print envelope.

No floats. Each module has a closed, sealed housing that holds air, trimmed with a little steel so it weighs 0.10 N in water and stands still on the tray. The parent's arm (500 g payload, a 2.45 N magnet) could not lift its own base in air (1.4 kg), but it can carry it under water. This is why the arm is put together under water, and why the water stands at 270 mm.

Face to face. The parent's tail leaves its head, turns round and docks face to face with the new tail. Its arm reaches into the new tail as it reaches into a head: the new arm's seat is 294 mm from its axis. It brings the four modules from a tray on the back glass one at a time and builds the arm upright in the seat. From the base on, the new arm has power from N's battery through the cuff and helps: it holds each joint where the parent can reach it.
After the handover the new tail has an arm, so it can pick up the rest itself: the last thing on the tray, a tile set, it takes with its own arm.
